primary_effectiveness_comparison.note: Raw failure events are NOT the primary success metric -- final orphans, orphan rate, retry recovery, and impacted Alphas are.
primary_effectiveness_comparison.interpretation: Evidence-stance orphan RATE improved marginally (100.0% -> 97.37%), driven by exactly ONE recovered call that succeeded on attempt 2 (not attempt 3) -- i.e. NOT causally attributable to the new fix. Absolute final-orphan COUNT and claims-orphaned both increased in raw terms, but this run also carries 6 more failed calls and a large one-off transport-error cluster (see below) that the pre-fix run did not have -- these two runs are not a controlled apples-to-apples comparison of identical underlying failure exposure. impacted_alpha_ids dropped from [A101] to [] this run, but this is because the specific claim that triggered A101's impact in the pre-fix run did not recur with an equivalent lineage here -- unrelated to evidence_stance_classifier (that impact channel is alpha_classifier-specific, per the prior audit's attribution-tool limitation).

third_attempt_analysis.conclusion: The 3rd attempt was genuinely exercised live 37 times in this run -- direct, real evidence the fix is ACTIVE in production -- but ZERO of those 37 calls recovered on attempt 3. This is not classified as failure per the task's own instruction ('if no call needed a third attempt, do not call that failure') because calls DID need and use the third attempt; the honest classification is that the opportunity was used but did not pay off in this specific run.
third_attempt_analysis.timeout_terminal_calls_note: 13 calls exhausted all 3 attempts via TIMEOUT -- consistent with, and not contradicting, the prior audit's own cautious 'POSSIBLY_RECOVERABLE, not proven' classification for this failure mode. This run adds real evidence that an un-modified 3rd attempt at the same 45s window did not, in these 13 cases, change the outcome.
third_attempt_analysis.transport_terminal_calls_note: 24 calls (72 raw evidence_stance events + 18 structure_extractor events = 90 total) exhausted all attempts via TRANSPORT_ERROR, ALL logged within a 1-2 SECOND window (23:48:08Z-23:48:09Z) at the very end of the run -- a brief, shared-infrastructure disruption event, structurally identical to (but larger than) the AMD transport cluster found in the prior audit. Because there is no backoff between attempts, 3 back-to-back fast-failing attempts fired inside the SAME 1-2 second outage window for every affected call -- a retry-COUNT increase without a backoff (Option F, explicitly deferred) cannot be expected to escape a brief outage this way. This event confounds roughly two-thirds (24 of 37) of this run's third-attempt trials and is NOT representative of steady-state conditions.

retry_benefit_classification.reasoning: 37 calls genuinely reached and used the new 3rd attempt (direct live confirmation the fix is active); none of them recovered. This does not meet CASE_R1 (no attempt-3 success), CASE_R3 (a real third-attempt opportunity DID occur, repeatedly), or CASE_R5 (no meaningful cost/latency/operational regression was found -- see below). CASE_R2 does not apply either: the orphan-rate improvement that did occur (100%->97.37%) is traceable to a single non-third-attempt recovery, so it is not even a 'directionally better, uncertain lineage' case -- the lineage is fully known and is NOT third-attempt-related.

latency_cost_observation.attribution_caveat: Not all wall-clock variance is attributable to the retry policy -- TradingAgents/Provider latency varies run-to-run for many unrelated reasons (already established throughout this whole session's TSM reproducibility findings). Of the +66 extra Provider attempts, 24 (the transport-error-cluster third attempts) failed near-instantly and consumed negligible wall-clock time; the other 13 (timeout-terminal third attempts) could each add up to ~45s, i.e. up to ~9.75 minutes theoretical maximum -- consistent with, and roughly explaining most of, the observed +5.16 minute total increase.
latency_cost_observation.classification_note: Neither risk is classified HIGH: the increase is bounded, scoped to already-failing calls, and consistent with the LOW pre-implementation estimate -- but it is also not INCONCLUSIVE, since a real, measurable (if modest and partly confounded) increase was directly observed.

keep_revert_recommendation.reasoning: Neither KEEP nor REVERT's stated criteria are cleanly met. KEEP requires 'bounded live evidence shows useful recovery or clearly improved final-orphan behavior without meaningful downside' -- no third-attempt recovery occurred, so no direct useful-recovery evidence exists; the modest orphan-rate improvement observed is not third-attempt-attributable. REVERT requires 'no useful recovery AND meaningful latency/cost downside or unexpected operational regression' -- the first half is true (no recovery), but the second half is not met (LOW-MEDIUM, not meaningful/unacceptable, cost/latency impact; no operational regression; no semantic change). Additionally, two-thirds of this run's third-attempt trials (24 of 37) were dominated by one brief, atypical transport-outage cluster that a retry-COUNT change alone was never expected to fix (that specific pattern needs Option F, not Option C) -- making this single run's third-attempt evidence base non-representative of steady-state conditions. Do not revert in this task per explicit instruction; this is a recommendation only.

next_development_step.reasoning: MSFT A304 was independently confirmed NOT Provider-caused in the prior Phase 2 recall recovery audit and reconfirmed again in the prior reliability audit (MSFT's impacted_alpha_ids=[A301], already a redundant Gold hit) -- this remains true regardless of the inconclusive live retry-fix result, since A304's own blocker is a regex/negation-aware extraction capability gap, unrelated to evidence_stance_classifier retry behavior.
